title: ProDG: Prototypes for Data-Free Generative Post-Hoc Explainability
claim: A frozen model's top channels select concept prompts that drive a generator to synthesize prototypes, yielding localized visual explanations without any data.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; pipeline on left, image grid right, rows labeled by channel
description: A large rounded cream container holds two sections. The left section, titled PROTOTYPE RETRIEVAL, has a green box at the top: an input beetle photo flows through a trapezoid Feature Extractor, a Disentanglement Module, a column of colored channel cells fully connected to a three-cell class output, with a 'Predicted Class' arrow and a purple dashed Top-k Relevant Channels Selection box. A purple arrow leads down to a pink Concept Prompt Bank. The bank has three circles labeled Channel 211, 384 and 369, each with a small beetle image and a concept tag (Insect Head Features, Antennae, Body Core). Colored arrows run from the circles into a dashed gold Generative Model box. The right section, titled EXPLANATION, is a 3x4 grid of beetle photos with yellow bounding boxes. Each row is labeled with a channel number (211, 384, 369), and the first column is the input image.
caption: \textbf{Overview of the \our{} prototype retrieval pipeline and explanation generation.} Given an input image, \our{} first applies a classification model to predict the target class. It then identifies the top-$k$ most influential channels with respect to the predicted class. From an optimized prompt bank, \our{} samples prompts to generate corresponding images, which are subsequently used to compute activation heatmaps and derive bounding boxes for visual explanations.
abstract: Ante-hoc interpretability methods based on prototypes provide highly accurate explanations by utilizing the intuitive "this looks like that" reasoning paradigm. On the other hand, post-hoc models can explain predictions for a single image without relying on an underlying dataset or requiring costly neural network retraining. Recent approaches successfully solve the retraining problem for prototype-based networks. However, they still face a fundamental limitation: they require access to a subset of data (e.g., a test or validation set) to search for and extract the visual prototypes. In this paper, we address this issue and introduce ProDG: Generative Prototypes for Data-Free Post-Hoc Explainability, a novel framework that leverages generative models to synthesize pure, high-fidelity prototypes directly from the frozen model's weights, completely eliminating the dependency on any external data. By establishing this new frontier in Data-Free XAI, ProDG unlocks robust visual interpretability for privacy-sensitive domains, where original data is strictly restricted or fundamentally inaccessible. Project page: https://github.com/piotr310100/ProDG
